title: Subcutaneous or intramuscular only, in single doses
rule_summary: A pharmacist or pharmacy intern may ONLY administer an eligible medication BY SUBCUTANEOUS OR INTRAMUSCULAR INJECTION, in accordance with manufacturer approved labeling and any risk evaluation and mitigation strategy requirements for the specific medication. The conditions on dispensing by administration include that administration is NOT INTRAVENOUS and that the medication is available in single-dose packaging and PRESCRIBED IN SINGLE DOSES, with or without refills.
exam_relevance: Tests the route limit and the separate single-dose condition, which candidates commonly merge into one idea about injections.

authority.name: Circular Letter DCP 26-03-124, Pharmacist Administration of Medications, 11 March 2026
authority.section: Administration and Dosing, with conditions (c) and (d) of Dispensing by Administration

authority.name: Massachusetts Department of Public Health regulations

exceptions: A prescription in single doses may carry refills
common_confusions: Treating any injection as permitted because the pharmacist is trained to inject
Assuming refills are prohibited, when single-dose prescribing may carry refills
Overlooking the manufacturer labeling and risk evaluation and mitigation strategy limits
